detail.longDescription: I have a Git repository with a local main master branch. I push the repository remotely to GitHub as origin . I created a new experimental branch exp from master , where new development will take place. I wish my team to collaborate on the experimental branch by pulling and pushing from/to GitHub, eventually merging exp to master . I was expecting git push origin master to include the new exp branch in GitHub, but that is not the case. Will git push origin exp make the experimental branch available in GitHub so that my team and I can pull, test, revise, push, and eventually merge? To clarify : my confusion arose in part from never having had the need for an experimetal branch to be accessible in GitHub. Now I need precisely that, so that my team and I can pull/push to tweak the project, while the master branch remains operational in GitHub. I have read branching and pushing as separate topics in the Git manual, but haven't found the intersection.
